'''Leon Pape''' (February 8, 1925 – January 2, 1984) was a [[medical physicist]] who received his [[BSc]], [[MSc]] (1953) and [[PhD]] (1965) in [[Physics]] from the [[University of Southern California]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.usc.edu/dept/physics/people/Alumni/P.html |title=Alumni: P |access-date=2013-03-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304091733/http://www.usc.edu/dept/physics/people/Alumni/P.html |archive-date=2016-03-04 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>Pape, L. (1953). Report on investigation of asymmetrical resonance pressure broadening of the helium lambda5875 line. ProQuest Dissertations And Theses; Thesis (M.S.)--University of Southern California, 1953.; Publication Number: AAT EP63371; Source: Masters Abstracts International, Volume: 54-01.; 45 p.</ref><ref>Pape, L. (1965). Investigation of Some Structurally Related Characteristics of the Urinary Glycoprotein of Tamm and Horsfall (Doctoral dissertation, University of Southern California).</ref>  He became certified in [[medical physics|radiological physics]] by the [[American Board of Radiology]] and from 1955 to 1962 he worked as a [[medical physicist|radiological physicist]] at the [[Cedars of Lebanon Hospital]] in [[Los Angeles]]. He served at the [http://www.calstatela.edu California State University Los Angeles] as [[radiation safety officer]] and as professor of physics until 1971, and worked on the development of studies in [[biophysics]], radiological [[health physics]], and [[electron microscopy]]. He was elevated to departmental head of physics at Cal State Los Angeles, and advocated with the California legislature to secure adequate funding for the [[Electrostatic nuclear accelerator|4-MeV Van de Graaf Laboratory]], unique to CSU system.  From 1971 until his death he worked at the [[August Krogh Institute]] at the [[University of Copenhagen]], [[Denmark]], in the zoophysiological laboratory. His central research area was membrane biophysics.<ref>Cohen, H. L., Morinigo, F. B., & [[Frieda Stahl|Stahl, F. A.]] (November 1984). Leon Pape. Physics Today, 37(11): 120-120.</ref>

==Leon Pape Memorial Lecture Series==
The Leon Pape Memorial Lecture Series was inaugurated by CSU after his "untimely death in January 1984 prompted the establishment of this lecture series in his memory, encompassing his many interests."<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.calstatela.edu/dept/physics/papelecture.htm |title=The Leon Pape Memorial Lectures |access-date=2013-03-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130204201723/http://www.calstatela.edu/dept/physics/papelecture.htm |archive-date=2013-02-04 |url-status=dead }}</ref>  The award of this Lectureship is highly prestigious,{{citation needed|date=March 2013}} with many Nobel Laureates and prominent academics having delivered it since its inception.
